analysis.title: GS FINS & REITs Daily (Alex Mitola, 17 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Overnight: E-minis +10bps, Nasdaq futures +50bps, US 10-year yield down slightly at 5.11%, crude +50bps after yesterday's sell-off. Markets are digesting the NVDA CEO news and its implications for the AI trade, including the company's financial support for the industry and additional chip export controls.
NVDA reports after the close on 11/17. The stock was +1% pre-market and the desk cites an implied earnings move of 8%.

Asia fell overnight after the US introduced new AI chip export controls covering Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia. Kioxia, Advantest, Softbank, Hynix, Samsung and Taiwan Semi were each down 2-5%. Europe was lower: FTSE -70bps, DAX -65bps, CAC -65bps, with energy outperforming and tech and consumer discretionary lagging.
VP Vance said the war in Iran 'wont become a forever war'. Crude was up slightly on otherwise quiet overnight news.

US data today: Retail Sales 8:30am, Industrial and Manufacturing Production 9:15am, NAHB Housing Market Index 10am. Fed speakers: Musalem 7:30am, Waller 9:10am, Hammack 9:30am, Williams 2:25pm. Pre-open earnings: AS, DIS, HD, VIK.

The S&P Financial Index closed -0.86% on the prior session, 7.8% above its 200-day moving average with a 14-day RSI of 58. 30% of S&P Financial stocks finished positive. Single-stock volumes were 20% below the 20-day average, while sector ETF volumes were about 15% higher.
Prior-session sector performance: P&C insurance, exchanges and life insurance outperformed. Alternative managers, asset managers and large-cap consumer finance lagged.
BAC: Berkshire Hathaway's 13F shows it sold about 27.5mn more BAC shares in Q3, roughly 1.3% of the quarter's traded volume, continuing a slow reduction of the position.

Consumer finance: GS analysts (Nash & Team) describe October credit as fairly benign. Formation rates continue to decline year over year at a moderating pace. Delinquency improvement is likely to keep slowing, but there should be some downward bias on delinquencies and losses. Loans grew about 5% YoY, with all issuers improving YoY except AXP. The desk thinks COF was particularly strong and says core COF trends may be improving.

Investment banking monitor: October announced IB activity fell 19% YoY and 25% MoM, driven by weaker M&A and DCM YoY, while ECM rose. YTD volumes are up 13% YoY (M&A +23%, ECM +60%, DCM +7%), versus +29%/+65%/+10% at end-September. Yaro & Team remain optimistic on the cycle, though leading indicators have weakened modestly.

MAA: 4Q blended pricing is expected to keep improving YoY (+40bps YoY in 3Q, +70bps in 2Q), with the 4Q sequential seasonal decline smaller than in 2025. Renewal increases average about 5.5% with 96% of 4Q decisions made. October occupancy was stable and new-lease pricing improved YoY for the first time in 2026.

MAA 2027 considerations: pricing expected to improve as supply declines in most markets, renewal pricing broadly in line with 2026, slightly positive earn-in, occupancy consistent with 2026, overhead within the historical 3-5% range, and acquisitions/dispositions slightly dilutive. $275-325mn of development funding is expected, with debt rising a further $400-500mn.

UDR: 1H27 blended lease rate growth is expected to be similar to the 4Q guide of 1.5%-2.0%. Market rents rose 50bps over the last 60 days versus -300bps a year ago. 80-100bps of same-store revenue earn-in is expected versus 0bps entering 2026. Apollo proceeds are expected to be accretive to 2027 FFOA.

CURB: quarter to date it has acquired 15 properties for $138.5M, funded with cash and forward equity settlement proceeds. Investment activity remains elevated and the pipeline gives visibility into closings through Q1 2027.
CUBE: same-store occupancy as of October 31 was 89.5%, +70bps YoY, versus +90bps YoY in September.

Housing Market Activity Scale for the week of Nov 8: up 2% sequentially, down 14% YoY, 33% below the long-term average. Purchase applications rose 7% and the mortgage rate fell 7bps to 7.11%. GIR channel checks suggest November activity remains weak.

Mizuho initiated a group of alternative and traditional asset managers: Outperform on BLK, APO, BX, KKR, ARES, OWL and IVZ, Underperform on TROW, Neutral on BEN and TPG. Texas Capital initiated VCTR at Buy.

GS equity outlook for 2027 (GIR): S&P 500 to rise 17% to 8,700 by year-end. EPS growth is forecast to slow from about 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. The forward P/E has fallen 19% in 2026 and is near its 10-year average. The base case holds P/E near 18x because of elevated rates and AI uncertainty. AI investment has lifted S&P earnings 25% above trend, and the 2028-and-beyond outlook is highly uncertain.

GS economists forecast 2027 global real GDP growth of 2.8% (2.7% in 2026) with downside risks, and expect inflation to slow. Their baseline is more dovish than market pricing, especially for the ECB (normalization cuts from 2027Q4). For the Fed they expect 25bp hikes in Dec 2026 and March 2027, then gradual cuts starting Nov 2027.
